articles.title: Tuning a Server for Benchmarking
articles.summary: Optimizing code starts with measuring it, and a measurement is only useful if it is repeatable: a 2% improvement is invisible under 5% of noise. Tuning for benchmarking is not the same as tuning for performance, but a noisy baseline is necessary for a benchmark to be useful. A benchmark wants the machine repeatable, even at the cost of some peak speed. A production box, however, wants every last bit of speed. A noisy baseline can be reduced by using techniques such as pause timing and resume timing to keep the sleep out of the measured time, and by using a DoNotOptimize flag to keep the result alive past the optimizer.

articles.title: Commodified Intelligence
articles.summary: Commodified Intelligence is a concept that refers to the idea that the value of human intellectual labor is rapidly decreasing due to the increasing use of artificial intelligence and automation. This can have negative consequences for workers, regardless of their occupation or level of education.
